subject.title: [Bug]: /hooks/agent silently drops accountId — hook dispatch bypasses cron normalization pipeline

question: Should maintainers wait for the open linked PR to be refreshed and proven, or replace it with a credited current-main fix for the hook `accountId` bug?
rationale: The issue is source-reproducible and has an open candidate fix, but the PR-side review shows missing real behavior proof and branch/architecture drift that automation should not bypass from the issue lane.

options.title: Refresh the linked PR
options.body: Ask the contributor to rebase the open PR onto current main, address review feedback, update docs, and add redacted real multi-account delivery proof.

options.title: Open a credited replacement
options.body: A maintainer or repair lane can rebuild the narrow fix on current main while crediting the issue and existing PR, then still require real behavior proof before merge.

options.title: Leave blocked
options.body: Keep the issue and linked PR open without new repair work until someone can provide a clean branch and live proof.

recommendation.title: Refresh the linked PR
recommendation.body: Ask the contributor to rebase the open PR onto current main, address review feedback, update docs, and add redacted real multi-account delivery proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent blame and GitHub metadata place vincentkoc closest to the current gateway hook payload and dispatch boundary.
